tasks.scope: Establish site boundaries, set up welfare facilities, confirm scaffold access routes via Kiora Lane and courtyard, establish occupant liaison procedures and communication protocols
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.1 — Construction work on or adjacent to road used by traffic
hazards: Trip hazard from welfare facility installation and temporary infrastructure on access routes
Vehicle strike — pedestrian movement via Kiora Lane shared with site traffic
Scaffold component delivery and staging on courtyard creating obstruction hazard
Communication breakdown between site team and building occupants leading to uncontrolled access during active work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Vehicle strike — pedestrian movement via Kiora Lane shared with site traffic
controls: Establish vehicle exclusion zone on Kiora Lane — erect 1.8 m high barricade and signage at lane entry and site boundary before any worker or delivery enters site.
Confirm scaffold access route through courtyard is clear of trip hazards — remove temporary infrastructure, measure clearances, photograph and record before scaffold components arrive.
Brief all site personnel and building occupants on vehicle movement protocol — one-way traffic on Kiora Lane, designated pedestrian crossing point, horn signal before each vehicle movement.
Install traffic control signage on Kiora Lane — 'Site Vehicle Access', 'Pedestrian Crossing', 'Reduced Speed' — positioned at 20 m intervals before site entry.
Establish occupant liaison point — named contact person on site, telephone number posted at all building entry points, daily briefing schedule displayed.
Stage scaffold components in designated courtyard zone — mark out with paint or tape, keep minimum 2 m clearance to building entry doors and pedestrian routes.
Check welfare facility location does not block or reduce access route width below 1.5 m — measure and record before installation.
Conduct site induction for all personnel — cover vehicle strike hazard, pedestrian protocol, occupant communication procedure, Kiora Lane one-way rule, emergency contact protocol.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any work activity until: vehicle exclusion barricade erected on Kiora Lane, signage installed, and occupant liaison contact details posted at all building entries.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle observed on Kiora Lane without designated spotter or horn signal.
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupant accesses site without briefing on active vehicle movement.
🛑 STOP WORK if: temporary infrastructure or scaffold components obstruct access route below 1.5 m width.
admin: Obtain EPA licence confirmation before any material delivery or site setup activity.
Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder — attach to site induction board.
Confirm all site personnel hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001).
Provide daily pre-start toolbox talk — cover vehicle movement on Kiora Lane, occupant communication protocol, change of conditions.
Record occupant liaison contact details and emergency response procedure — post at main site office and welfare facility.
Photograph site boundaries, barricade location, and access routes — file for compliance record.
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest (Day/Night compliant) — wear during all site entry and pedestrian movement on Kiora Lane.
Safety helmet — wear when moving through courtyard during scaffold component staging.
steel-capped footwear— wear on site access routes to reduce trip hazard exposure.

monitoring.critical_control: Vehicle exclusion barricade remains erect and signage visible always during site setup.
monitoring.frequency: Before each site entry, daily at start of shift, before each vehicle movement
monitoring.evidence: Photograph of barricade and signage, induction register signed by all personnel, occupant liaison contact log, daily traffic movement record

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to balconies and working levels
tasks.scope: Erect working scaffold to service all balcony work areas, including edge protection, work platforms, and fall protection above 4m height. Secure scaffold against balcony structures
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold platform collapse or edge protection failure during erection above 4m
Fall from height — incomplete bracing or securing of scaffold against balcony structures during assembly
Dropped object — scaffold components, fittings, or tools striking occupants or workers below during erection
Entrapment or crush — fingers or limbs caught during scaffold frame assembly and clamp tightening
Inadequate scaffold design or unauthorised modification reducing fall arrest capacity
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — scaffold platform collapse or edge protection failure during erection above 4m
controls: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component placement commences.
Confirm load calculations and scaffold design match site conditions, balcony attachment points, and fall heights above 4m.
Install edge protection (guardrail or compliant barrier) to all working platforms as scaffold frame is erected — do not leave any platform unguarded.
Secure scaffold bracing and ties to balcony structures using engineer-approved fixings — tighten all clamps fully and test by hand before platform use.
Isolate drop zones below scaffold erection area with barricade and signage — prohibit occupant and worker access during assembly.
Check all frame connections, cross-braces, and platform boards for damage or misalignment before workers stand on platform.
Wear fall arrest harness clipped to anchor point when erecting or modifying scaffold above 4m — anchor must be independent of scaffold being erected.
Obtain handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder confirming scaffold compliance before any worker uses completed scaffold.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to scaffold platform until: licenced scaffolder has inspected all connections, bracing, and ties, and signed handover certificate confirming fall protection compliance.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold above 4m without: engineer-approved design and load calculations verified by PM.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold frame connection is loose, bent, or missing — re-check and repair before use resumes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection or guardrail is damaged, incomplete, or below 1.1m height — replace or repair before platform work continues.
🛑 STOP WORK if: bracing or ties securing scaffold to balcony structures are visibly bent, cracked, or partially detached — halt all work and reinforce before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: make sure licenced scaffolder (class appropriate to height and load) supervises and signs all scaffold erection phases.
Confirm working at heights permit is issued and sighted by all workers before elevated work starts.
Record scaffold handover certificate and load calculations on site file before commencement.
tell building occupants of erection schedule and drop zone barricade locations to minimise impact on occupied areas.
Conduct toolbox talk covering scaffold access, fall arrest harness use, and stop-work triggers before first shift on scaffold.
ppe: Hard hat — worn when near scaffold erection area (overhead hazard from components and tools).
High-visibility clothing — worn by all workers during scaffold assembly to make sure visibility to occupants and other trades.
steel-capped footwear— worn with ankle support for stability on scaffold platforms and during tie-off work.
Fall arrest harness and lanyard with energy absorber — worn and clipped to independent anchor when erecting or working above 4m.
cut-resistant gloves

monitoring.critical_control: Licenced scaffolder checks all frame connections and bracing are fully tightened and clipped before platform occupancy.
monitoring.frequency: Before each platform level opens to workers; daily visual check thereafter until scaffold removal.
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate signed by scaffolder; photographic record of completed edge protection and bracing; toolbox talk sign-in sheet.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane and screed
tasks.scope: Strip existing waterproofing membrane and screed layer from all balcony surfaces to expose substrate. Manage silica dust and debris. Dispose of removed materials off-site
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust during cutting, grinding, or pneumatic removal of screed and membrane
Eye injury from dust and airborne debris during dry removal methods
Slip hazard from wet debris and waterproofing residue on balcony surfaces during stripping
Cut or laceration from membrane edges, broken tiles, or exposed substrate debris
Soft tissue strain from repetitive scraping, prying, and manual removal of adhesive and membrane
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust during cutting, grinding, or pneumatic removal of screed and membrane
controls: Wet down membrane and screed surfaces with water mist before cutting or grinding to suppress airborne silica dust.
Use dust extraction equipment with HEPA filtration connected to all power tools during cutting, grinding, or pneumatic removal.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and checked before starting dust-generating work; replace cartridge after 4 hours or if resistance increases.
Barricade balcony perimeter to exclude non-essential workers during dry debris removal and dust generation.
Collect and contain all screed and membrane waste in sealed bins on-site before removal to prevent dust escape during transport.
Check slip resistance of work surface before each task start; apply anti-slip tape or matting over wet debris areas.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (nitrile-coated minimum) when handling membrane edges, broken tiles, and adhesive debris.
Rotate workers off scraping and manual removal tasks every 60 minutes to reduce repetitive strain; alternate with other site tasks.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start membrane removal until: scaffold handover certificate signed and dust extraction system tested operational.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove waste from site until: all bins sealed and load checked against site waste manifest.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction equipment fails or becomes disconnected during grinding or cutting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker removes respirator or dust mask during active dust-generating work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: slip hazard from water/debris creates uncontrolled movement risk on balcony surface.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain copy of waterproofing product SDS before work start; brief team on hazard warnings and PPE match.
Establish dust monitoring protocol — supervisor to follow dust generation visually each hour; stop work if visible dust exceeds workspace containment.
Schedule work to avoid peak occupancy times in building; tell building manager of dust suppression method and expected duration.
Record waste collection and manifest for off-site disposal; retain evidence of licensed waste contractor receipt.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (fitted and checked each use)
eye protection
chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
hi-viz shirt or vest
steel-capped footwear
High-visibility vest (for scaffold access and site movement)

monitoring.critical_control: Check dust extraction system running and connected before each tool use; test airflow at nozzle.
monitoring.frequency: before each tool start and every 60 minutes during active work
monitoring.evidence: visual inspection of dust extraction operation; supervisor log of checks; P2 cartridge change dates recorded

tasks.scope: On Leo and Associates approval, excavate and seal cracks in concrete slab using approved sealant or injection method. Repair spalling and exposed reinforcement. Allow curing per specification before proceeding
hazards: Exposure to chemical hazards during excavation and injection of sealant or curing compounds — vapour inhalation and skin contact
Dust generation during crack excavation and preparation of substrate
Eye splash or skin burn from injection resin or epoxy sealant during application
Inadequate surface preparation or sealed defects during cure period leading to waterproofing failure — latent rework risk
tasks.dominant_hazard: Exposure to chemical hazards during excavation and injection of sealant or curing compounds — vapour inhalation and skin contact
controls: Obtain Leo and Associates written approval before starting crack excavation or injection work.
Check SDS for sealant or injection product and brief all workers on vapour hazards and skin contact risks before use.
Wet excavation area with water spray to suppress dust during crack preparation and debris removal.
Use respiratory protective equipment (half-mask P2 or equivalent) during crack excavation and injection application.
Apply sealant or injection resin in well-ventilated area or use site-supplied ventilation to direct vapours away from workers.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Barricade work area to prevent occupants or other workers contacting wet sealant or curing material.
Allow curing time per product specification and site conditions before removing barricades or allowing foot traffic.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant or injection resin until: Leo and Associates has signed off crack location and repair method
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or remove barricades until: curing period specified on product SDS or site specification is complete and verified by supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker shows signs of chemical vapour exposure (dizziness, headache, skin irritation) — move to fresh air and tell supervisor immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: sealant or injection material contacts occupants or unprotected skin — stop application, provide first aid, and review containment control
🛑 STOP WORK if: environmental conditions (rain, wind, temperature below product specification) prevent proper cure — do not proceed until conditions restore
admin: tell building occupants of crack repair work schedule and barricaded areas before start.
Record Leo and Associates approval sign-off on site documentation before crack excavation begins.
Record actual curing time and completion date on defect register or handover documentation.
Brief all workers on sealant SDS, hazard symbols, and first-aid response before product first use on site.

chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
eye protection
High-visibility vest (occupied building context)

monitoring.frequency: before each rectification session
monitoring.evidence: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site

tasks.scope: On Leo and Associates approval of repaired substrate, apply new waterproofing membrane to all balcony surfaces including perimeters, joints, and penetrations. Apply according to manufacturer specification and hold point conditions
hazards: Exposure to chemical vapours and isocyanates during application of liquid waterproofing membrane — respiratory sensitisation and skin irritation
Slip hazard on wet membrane application and slippery cured surface before screed application
Chemical burn or irritation to eyes and skin from spill or splatter of membrane material
Inadequate ventilation on occupied building balconies during solvent-based or two-part membrane application
Application defect or poor adhesion to substrate or cracks — leading to latent waterproofing failure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Exposure to chemical vapours and isocyanates during application of liquid waterproofing membrane — respiratory sensitisation and skin irritation
controls: Obtain and review SDS for membrane product before work starts — identify flash point, VOC content, PPE requirements, and first aid.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across balcony work area — extract vapours away from workers and occupied spaces below.
Apply membrane only during low wind conditions — wind speed under 15 km/h to prevent vapour drift into occupied spaces.
Wear respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum for solvent vapours; upgrade to organic vapour cartridge if isocyanate-based product.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves — nitrile minimum; upgrade to butyl if isocyanate exposure confirmed on SDS.
Wear eye protection— eye protection; chemical splash eye protection
Mix two-part membranes in separate mixing area upwind — do not mix on balcony work surface.
Apply membrane in thin uniform coats — follow manufacturer specification for coverage rate and dry time between coats.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: Leo and Associates provides written approval of repaired substrate and sign-off on substrate preparation report.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next coat or screed application until: previous membrane layer has cured to manufacturer specification time — check cure time against temperature and humidity on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or weather turns wet — reposition workers and halt application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection is damaged, fogging, or inadequate seal — withdraw worker and replace mask.
🛑 STOP WORK if: membrane adhesion to substrate is visibly poor or membrane is lifting at edges on test patch — investigate substrate defect and halt until root cause is resolved.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm SDS training completed for all workers on membrane product — record name, date, and trainer on site sign-in.
Brief occupants before work — tell of work hours, chemical odour, balcony closure, and ventilation requirements.
Record ambient temperature and humidity before and after each application — verify conditions meet manufacturer specification.
Photograph substrate condition pre-application and test patch bond at 24 hours — attach to SWMS handover file.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and current before balcony work starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day

chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
eye protection
hi-viz shirt or vest

monitoring.frequency: before each shift start
monitoring.evidence: SDS visible at work station, correct gloves/respirator worn, ventilation adequate
monitoring.what_to_look_for: SDS visible at work station, correct gloves/respirator worn, ventilation adequate

tasks.scope: Apply screed layer to all membraned surfaces. Set tile bed and install new tiles to all balcony surfaces. Grout and seal all joints. Install base trims and skirting
hazards: Slip and fall hazard during screed application on balcony slopes and around joints — wet surface and working at height
Dust generation during tile cutting, grinding of grout, and joint preparation
Musculoskeletal injury from manual handling of tiles, tile bed, and screed materials
Chemical exposure during grout and sealant application — skin contact and inhalation
Incomplete or poor tile adhesion and joint sealing — latent water ingress and membrane breach risk
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip and fall hazard during screed application on balcony slopes and around joints — wet surface and working at height
controls: Wet all screed surfaces with water mist before application to reduce dust generation.
Apply screed in thin layers — maximum 20mm per pass — to prevent slumping on slopes.
Install edge protection and anti-slip matting on all wet screed surfaces before worker access.
Cut tiles over a water tray or wet saw — do not dry cut on balcony surfaces.
Wear dust mask (P2) during tile cutting, grout grinding, and joint preparation.
Set tiles using tile bed mixed to manufacturers specification — check consistency before each batch.
Grout all joints within 24 hours of tile setting — do not leave gaps ungrouted overnight.
Apply sealant per SDS — make sure substrate is clean and dry before application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not grout tiles until: tile bed is set firm (minimum 24 hours) and site supervisor confirms visual inspection of all tile adhesion
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not seal joints until: grout is fully cured (manufacturer specification — typically 7 days) and moisture testing confirms substrate is dry
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: rain or high wind forecast within 48 hours of grout application — cover exposed work with plastic sheeting
🛑 STOP WORK if: any tile shows hollow sound on tap test — remove, clean substrate, and reset using fresh tile bed
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker slips or near-miss occurs on wet surface — review slip prevention matting and reposition access routes
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display working at heights permit (signed by site supervisor) before any worker accesses balcony.
Verify scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and displayed at entry point.
Review SDS for screed, tile bed, grout, and sealant products at toolbox before task start.
Record tile adhesion test results (tape pull or hammer tap) — supervisor to sign daily.
tell building occupants 48 hours before work — advise balcony access restrictions during wet phase.
Conduct noise management briefing if grout grinding occurs — confirm hearing protection fit.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day

Safety harness and shock-absorbing lanyard (attached to secure fixed point — not scaffold only)
Non-slip boots with good ankle support (water and chemical resistant preferred)

chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
Eye protection (eye protection

monitoring.frequency: Before each shift and after any rain or delay

hazards: Fall from height during balustrade reinstallation and testing — incomplete edge protection if scaffold removed early
Dropped object — balustrade components, fixings, or tools striking occupants or workers below
Entrapment hazard during balustrade frame assembly and fastening
Chemical exposure during sealant and penetration sealing application
Inadequate structural integrity of balustrade reinstallation or balcony fixings — latent structural failure risk
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during balustrade reinstallation and testing — incomplete edge protection if scaffold removed early
controls: Verify scaffold remains in place and tagged safe before starting balustrade work.
Check all balustrade components for damage, corrosion, or missing fixings before installation.
Install edge protection netting or barriers on scaffold to catch dropped fixings and tools.
Apply sealant only in dry conditions with natural ventilation or mechanical extraction active.
Review SDS for sealant product and brief all workers on chemical hazards before opening containers.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and respiratory protection when applying membrane sealants in enclosed balcony areas.
Do not remove or lower scaffold sections until all balustrade fixings are complete and load-tested.
Test drainage outlets by pouring water and confirming flow — do not assume gravity drainage works.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install balustrade fixings until: structural engineer confirms balcony substrate integrity and bearing capacity for reinstalled components.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove or lower scaffold until: supervisor verifies all balustrade fixings torqued to specification and drainage tested and functioning.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade component shows movement, cracking, or loose fixings during or after installation.

tasks.task: Expose and prepare substrate for inspection
tasks.scope: Remove remaining tile bed and adhesive to expose full substrate. Clean and prepare slab surface. Photograph and document all cracks and defects. tell Leo and Associates for inspection hold point
hazards: Exposure of asbestos-containing tile adhesive or membrane during removal of remaining tile bed — inhalation or disturbance risk
Dust generation during final cleaning and surface preparation of exposed concrete
Fall hazard on unstable or uneven exposed substrate during inspection and photography
Soft tissue injury from manual scraping and cleaning of substrate surface
tasks.dominant_hazard: Exposure of asbestos-containing tile adhesive or membrane during removal of remaining tile bed — inhalation or disturbance risk
controls: Stop work and isolate area immediately if tile adhesive or membrane appears discoloured, friable, or crumbly — photograph and tell supervisor before touching.
Wet-spray all tile bed and adhesive residue with water mist before scraping to suppress dust — reapply every 15 minutes during removal.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (fitted) + eye protection, grinding, and surface preparation work — change mask when damp or blocked.
Use hand scraper or soft wire brush — not power grinder or jackhammer — to remove adhesive and tile bed residue.
Seal exposed substrate edges and penetrations with duct tape immediately after cleaning to prevent water ingress during hold period.
Photograph all substrate defects, cracks, and staining before final cleaning — include scale and compass direction in each frame.
Document photographic record with date, time, location grid, and defect reference number on site inspection sheet.
Verify concrete surface is dry and stable before Leo and Associates site inspection — confirm substrate temperature above 10°C.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to waterproofing application until: Leo and Associates certifies substrate condition and approves defect rectification plan in writing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is confirmed or suspected — do not disturb further; tell supervisor and EPA-licensed asbestos assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate shows active water seepage, deep structural cracking (>2mm), or spalling — do not proceed until engineer assessment completed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker experiences respiratory symptoms, coughing, or breathing difficulty — remove from area and seek medical advice.
admin: Obtain EPA asbestos licence holder clearance before starting tile bed removal — retain copy on site.
Brief all workers on asbestos disturbance triggers and stop-work procedure before task start.
Record substrate condition photographs and defect locations in site diary with date and time.
tell Leo and Associates 24 hours before hold point to schedule inspection — confirm attendance before final cleaning.
Retain all documentation and photographs with project file pending waterproofing approval.

hazards: Fall hazard during final inspection on wet or contaminated balcony surfaces with incomplete remedial work
Slippery surfaces during photography and walkover inspection of tiled or grouted balconies
Exposure to incompletely cured sealants or grout during final inspection — contact hazard and chemical exposure
Defects or non-conformances not identified during inspection leading to premature handover and latent failure
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall hazard during final inspection on wet or contaminated balcony surfaces with incomplete remedial work
controls: Check balcony surface for wet, algae, loose debris or uncured sealant before starting inspection.
Dry contaminated surfaces with clean cloths or allow sealant to cure per SDS before inspection begins.
Wear non-slip footwear with grip soles on all tiled, grouted or treated balcony surfaces.
Use handrails or edge protection always — do not lean over balcony edges during photography.
Brief Leo and Associates inspector on incomplete remedial work zones before walkover starts.
Photograph completed works from safe positions — do not stand on unstable or wet surfaces.
Document each defect or non-conformance with photo and location — do not proceed to repair without written approval.
fix defects using same material and method as original work — verify SDS and cure times before sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start final inspection until: balcony surface is dry and all sealants or grout have cured per product SDS, verified by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not request handover sign-off until: Leo and Associates inspector has checked all defects and approved rectification method in writing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: surface becomes wet or contaminated during inspection — cease walkover and dry or allow cure before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: uncured sealant, grout or chemical residue is present on balcony — establish cure time from SDS and re-schedule inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: defect identified poses immediate safety risk to occupants or workers — cease rectification and tell supervisor and inspector before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

hazards: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling above 4m — loss of edge protection as scaffold removed sequentially
Dropped object — scaffold components, clamps, and bracing striking workers or occupants below during disassembly
Crush or entrapment hazard during removal of clamps, frames, and bracing connections
Unstable scaffold frame or incomplete bracing during phased dismantling — collapse risk

hazards: Exposure of asbestos-containing tile adhesive or membrane during removal of remaining tile bed — inhalation or disturbance risk
Dust generation during final cleaning and surface preparation of exposed concrete
Fall hazard on unstable or uneven exposed substrate during inspection and photography
Soft tissue injury from manual scraping and cleaning of substrate surface
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Exposure of asbestos-containing tile adhesive or membrane during removal of remaining tile bed — inhalation or disturbance risk
controls: Stop work and isolate area immediately if tile adhesive or membrane appears discoloured, friable, or crumbly — photograph and tell supervisor before touching.
Wet-spray all tile bed and adhesive residue with water mist before scraping to suppress dust — reapply every 15 minutes during removal.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (fitted) + eye protection, grinding, and surface preparation work — change mask when damp or blocked.
Use hand scraper or soft wire brush — not power grinder or jackhammer — to remove adhesive and tile bed residue.
Seal exposed substrate edges and penetrations with duct tape immediately after cleaning to prevent water ingress during hold period.
Photograph all substrate defects, cracks, and staining before final cleaning — include scale and compass direction in each frame.
Document photographic record with date, time, location grid, and defect reference number on site inspection sheet.
Verify concrete surface is dry and stable before Leo and Associates site inspection — confirm substrate temperature above 10°C.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to waterproofing application until: Leo and Associates certifies substrate condition and approves defect rectification plan in writing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is confirmed or suspected — do not disturb further; tell supervisor and EPA-licensed asbestos assessor immediately.
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate shows active water seepage, deep structural cracking (>2mm), or spalling — do not proceed until engineer assessment completed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker experiences respiratory symptoms, coughing, or breathing difficulty — remove from area and seek medical advice.
admin: Obtain EPA asbestos licence holder clearance before starting tile bed removal — retain copy on site.
Brief all workers on asbestos disturbance triggers and stop-work procedure before task start.
Record substrate condition photographs and defect locations in site diary with date and time.
tell Leo and Associates 24 hours before hold point to schedule inspection — confirm attendance before final cleaning.
Retain all documentation and photographs with project file pending waterproofing approval.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) (fitted to face — not valved respirator) during scraping and cleaning phases
eye protection— splash/dust rated
chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
hi-viz shirt or vest
steel-capped footwear— slip resistant

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.who: Supervisor + EPA-licensed asbestos spotter on first 2 hours
monitoring.frequency: continuous during removal phase; visual check every 30 minutes during cleaning
monitoring.evidence: Site diary note of adhesive condition; photograph of surface type; supervisor sign-off that no friable/suspected asbestos disturbed

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Expose and prepare substrate for
responsibility.WKR: Perform Expose and prepare substrate for per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: On Leo and Associates approval, excavate and seal cracks in concrete slab using approved sealant or injection method. Repair spalling and exposed reinforcement. Allow curing per specification before proceeding
hazards: Exposure to chemical hazards during excavation and injection of sealant or curing compounds — vapour inhalation and skin contact
Dust generation during crack excavation and preparation of substrate
Eye splash or skin burn from injection resin or epoxy sealant during application
Inadequate surface preparation or sealed defects during cure period leading to waterproofing failure — latent rework risk
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Exposure to chemical hazards during excavation and injection of sealant or curing compounds — vapour inhalation and skin contact
controls: Obtain Leo and Associates written approval before starting crack excavation or injection work.
Check SDS for sealant or injection product and brief all workers on vapour hazards and skin contact risks before use.
Wet excavation area with water spray to suppress dust during crack preparation and debris removal.
Use respiratory protective equipment (half-mask P2 or equivalent) during crack excavation and injection application.
Apply sealant or injection resin in well-ventilated area or use site-supplied ventilation to direct vapours away from workers.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Barricade work area to prevent occupants or other workers contacting wet sealant or curing material.
Allow curing time per product specification and site conditions before removing barricades or allowing foot traffic.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant or injection resin until: Leo and Associates has signed off crack location and repair method
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or remove barricades until: curing period specified on product SDS or site specification is complete and verified by supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker shows signs of chemical vapour exposure (dizziness, headache, skin irritation) — move to fresh air and tell supervisor immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: sealant or injection material contacts occupants or unprotected skin — stop application, provide first aid, and review containment control
🛑 STOP WORK if: environmental conditions (rain, wind, temperature below product specification) prevent proper cure — do not proceed until conditions restore
admin: tell building occupants of crack repair work schedule and barricaded areas before start.
Record Leo and Associates approval sign-off on site documentation before crack excavation begins.
Record actual curing time and completion date on defect register or handover documentation.
Brief all workers on sealant SDS, hazard symbols, and first-aid response before product first use on site.
ppe: Half-mask respirator P2 (or equivalent) for excavation and injection application
chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
eye protection
High-visibility vest (occupied building context)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each rectification session
monitoring.evidence: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Signed defect list, photographic record, specification document on site

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.scope: On Leo and Associates approval of repaired substrate, apply new waterproofing membrane to all balcony surfaces including perimeters, joints, and penetrations. Apply according to manufacturer specification and hold point conditions
hazards: Exposure to chemical vapours and isocyanates during application of liquid waterproofing membrane — respiratory sensitisation and skin irritation
Slip hazard on wet membrane application and slippery cured surface before screed application
Chemical burn or irritation to eyes and skin from spill or splatter of membrane material
Inadequate ventilation on occupied building balconies during solvent-based or two-part membrane application
Application defect or poor adhesion to substrate or cracks — leading to latent waterproofing failure
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Exposure to chemical vapours and isocyanates during application of liquid waterproofing membrane — respiratory sensitisation and skin irritation
controls: Obtain and review SDS for membrane product before work starts — identify flash point, VOC content, PPE requirements, and first aid.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across balcony work area — extract vapours away from workers and occupied spaces below.
Apply membrane only during low wind conditions — wind speed under 15 km/h to prevent vapour drift into occupied spaces.
Wear respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum for solvent vapours; upgrade to organic vapour cartridge if isocyanate-based product.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves — nitrile minimum; upgrade to butyl if isocyanate exposure confirmed on SDS.
Wear eye protection— eye protection; chemical splash eye protection
Mix two-part membranes in separate mixing area upwind — do not mix on balcony work surface.
Apply membrane in thin uniform coats — follow manufacturer specification for coverage rate and dry time between coats.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: Leo and Associates provides written approval of repaired substrate and sign-off on substrate preparation report.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next coat or screed application until: previous membrane layer has cured to manufacturer specification time — check cure time against temperature and humidity on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or weather turns wet — reposition workers and halt application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respiratory protection is damaged, fogging, or inadequate seal — withdraw worker and replace mask.
🛑 STOP WORK if: membrane adhesion to substrate is visibly poor or membrane is lifting at edges on test patch — investigate substrate defect and halt until root cause is resolved.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm SDS training completed for all workers on membrane product — record name, date, and trainer on site sign-in.
Brief occupants before work — tell of work hours, chemical odour, balcony closure, and ventilation requirements.
Record ambient temperature and humidity before and after each application — verify conditions meet manufacturer specification.
Photograph substrate condition pre-application and test patch bond at 24 hours — attach to SWMS handover file.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and current before balcony work starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: P2 particulate mask or organic vapour cartridge respirator (upgrade if isocyanate product confirmed)
chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
eye protection
hi-viz shirt or vest
steel-capped footwear

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start
monitoring.evidence: SDS visible at work station, correct gloves/respirator worn, ventilation adequate
monitoring.what_to_look_for: SDS visible at work station, correct gloves/respirator worn, ventilation adequate

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Apply waterproofing membrane system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply screed layer to all membraned surfaces. Set tile bed and install new tiles to all balcony surfaces. Grout and seal all joints. Install base trims and skirting
hazards: Slip and fall hazard during screed application on balcony slopes and around joints — wet surface and working at height
Dust generation during tile cutting, grinding of grout, and joint preparation
Musculoskeletal injury from manual handling of tiles, tile bed, and screed materials
Chemical exposure during grout and sealant application — skin contact and inhalation
Incomplete or poor tile adhesion and joint sealing — latent water ingress and membrane breach risk
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Slip and fall hazard during screed application on balcony slopes and around joints — wet surface and working at height
controls: Wet all screed surfaces with water mist before application to reduce dust generation.
Apply screed in thin layers — maximum 20mm per pass — to prevent slumping on slopes.
Install edge protection and anti-slip matting on all wet screed surfaces before worker access.
Cut tiles over a water tray or wet saw — do not dry cut on balcony surfaces.
Wear dust mask (P2) during tile cutting, grout grinding, and joint preparation.
Set tiles using tile bed mixed to manufacturers specification — check consistency before each batch.
Grout all joints within 24 hours of tile setting — do not leave gaps ungrouted overnight.
Apply sealant per SDS — make sure substrate is clean and dry before application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not grout tiles until: tile bed is set firm (minimum 24 hours) and site supervisor confirms visual inspection of all tile adhesion
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not seal joints until: grout is fully cured (manufacturer specification — typically 7 days) and moisture testing confirms substrate is dry
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: rain or high wind forecast within 48 hours of grout application — cover exposed work with plastic sheeting
🛑 STOP WORK if: any tile shows hollow sound on tap test — remove, clean substrate, and reset using fresh tile bed
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker slips or near-miss occurs on wet surface — review slip prevention matting and reposition access routes
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display working at heights permit (signed by site supervisor) before any worker accesses balcony.
Verify scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and displayed at entry point.
Review SDS for screed, tile bed, grout, and sealant products at toolbox before task start.
Record tile adhesion test results (tape pull or hammer tap) — supervisor to sign daily.
tell building occupants 48 hours before work — advise balcony access restrictions during wet phase.
Conduct noise management briefing if grout grinding occurs — confirm hearing protection fit.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Hard hat (on-site standard — balcony edge hazard)
Safety harness and shock-absorbing lanyard (attached to secure fixed point — not scaffold only)
Non-slip boots with good ankle support (water and chemical resistant preferred)
Dust mask P2 (during tile cutting, grout grinding, joint preparation)
chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or task-appropriate)
Eye protection (eye protection
High-visibility vest (occupied building — visibility to other trades and occupants)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift and after any rain or delay
monitoring.evidence: Daily toolbox log — date, worker initials, matting condition sign-off; photographic record of matting placement

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed and retile balconies
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed and retile balconies per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Reinstall or repair balustrade fixings, drainage outlets, and other balcony fittings. Seal all penetrations and connections. Test drainage function and document completion
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during balustrade reinstallation and testing — incomplete edge protection if scaffold removed early
Dropped object — balustrade components, fixings, or tools striking occupants or workers below
Entrapment hazard during balustrade frame assembly and fastening
Chemical exposure during sealant and penetration sealing application
Inadequate structural integrity of balustrade reinstallation or balcony fixings — latent structural failure risk
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during balustrade reinstallation and testing — incomplete edge protection if scaffold removed early
controls: Verify scaffold remains in place and tagged safe before starting balustrade work.
Check all balustrade components for damage, corrosion, or missing fixings before installation.
Install edge protection netting or barriers on scaffold to catch dropped fixings and tools.
Apply sealant only in dry conditions with natural ventilation or mechanical extraction active.
Review SDS for sealant product and brief all workers on chemical hazards before opening containers.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and respiratory protection when applying membrane sealants in enclosed balcony areas.
Do not remove or lower scaffold sections until all balustrade fixings are complete and load-tested.
Test drainage outlets by pouring water and confirming flow — do not assume gravity drainage works.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install balustrade fixings until: structural engineer confirms balcony substrate integrity and bearing capacity for reinstalled components.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove or lower scaffold until: supervisor verifies all balustrade fixings torqued to specification and drainage tested and functioning.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade component shows movement, cracking, or loose fixings during or after installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: sealant application occurs in wet conditions or with inadequate ventilation — chemical absorption and cure failure risk.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold tag is removed or handover certificate not present before any elevated work starts.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit and handover certificate before starting work.
Confirm working at heights permit signed by responsible person and displayed on site.
Obtain current SDS for sealant product and store on site — accessible to all workers.
Brief all workers on balcony fall risk, dropped object hazards, and chemical exposure before work starts.
Record all drainage tests and balustrade completion photographs in site diary or digital record.
tell building occupants of work schedule and exclusion zones to prevent access during elevated tasks.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Hard hat with chin strap (protection against dropped objects and struck-by hazards).
Safety harness and lanyard anchored to independent fixed point — not balustrade under test.
cut-resistant gloves
eye protection
High-visibility vest or jacket.
Steel-capped boots with good grip.

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm scaffold tag present and balustrade fixings torqued to specification before worker access.
monitoring.frequency: before each shift and before moving to new balcony section
monitoring.evidence: Scaffold tag inspection record and torque test record (mechanical check or calibrated wrench log).

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

task_blocks_raw.scope: Carry out final inspection with Leo and Associates. Photograph completed works. fix any defects or non-conformances before handover. Obtain sign-off documentation
hazards: Fall hazard during final inspection on wet or contaminated balcony surfaces with incomplete remedial work
Slippery surfaces during photography and walkover inspection of tiled or grouted balconies
Exposure to incompletely cured sealants or grout during final inspection — contact hazard and chemical exposure
Defects or non-conformances not identified during inspection leading to premature handover and latent failure
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall hazard during final inspection on wet or contaminated balcony surfaces with incomplete remedial work
controls: Check balcony surface for wet, algae, loose debris or uncured sealant before starting inspection.
Dry contaminated surfaces with clean cloths or allow sealant to cure per SDS before inspection begins.
Wear non-slip footwear with grip soles on all tiled, grouted or treated balcony surfaces.
Use handrails or edge protection always — do not lean over balcony edges during photography.
Brief Leo and Associates inspector on incomplete remedial work zones before walkover starts.
Photograph completed works from safe positions — do not stand on unstable or wet surfaces.
Document each defect or non-conformance with photo and location — do not proceed to repair without written approval.
fix defects using same material and method as original work — verify SDS and cure times before sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start final inspection until: balcony surface is dry and all sealants or grout have cured per product SDS, verified by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not request handover sign-off until: Leo and Associates inspector has checked all defects and approved rectification method in writing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: surface becomes wet or contaminated during inspection — cease walkover and dry or allow cure before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: uncured sealant, grout or chemical residue is present on balcony — establish cure time from SDS and re-schedule inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: defect identified poses immediate safety risk to occupants or workers — cease rectification and tell supervisor and inspector before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate is current and signed by licenced scaffolder before inspection starts.
Verify working at heights permit is current and signed before each elevated task.
Brief all inspectors and rectification workers on occupied building constraints — no noise or disturbance outside agreed hours.
Establish defect log with Leo and Associates — photograph, location, cause, rectification method and sign-off required for each item.
Schedule rectification works to minimise occupant impact — coordinate with building manager on access and timing.
Confirm all workers hold current White Card induction and remedial task competency before starting.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Non-slip footwear with grip sole
High-visibility vest
eye protection

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: continuous during inspection and rectification
monitoring.evidence: Site log — surface condition checked and documented; defect log with photos and sign-offs; handover certificate filed.

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle working scaffold in reverse order of erection. Remove all edge protection and bracing. Clear scaffold components from site. Make good access routes
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling above 4m — loss of edge protection as scaffold removed sequentially
Dropped object — scaffold components, clamps, and bracing striking workers or occupants below during disassembly
Crush or entrapment hazard during removal of clamps, frames, and bracing connections
Unstable scaffold frame or incomplete bracing during phased dismantling — collapse risk
Inadequate or missing fall protection during final dismantling stages — unsecured working edges
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling above 4m — loss of edge protection as scaffold removed sequentially
controls: Obtain signed scaffold dismantling permit from licenced scaffolder before starting work.
Establish exclusion zone 6m radius around scaffold base — barricade and signage, no occupants or workers below.
Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and fall protection requirements before each shift.
Wear full-body harness and lanyard clipped to independent anchor point above working position throughout dismantling.
Dismantle in reverse order of erection — remove edge protection only after securing alternative fall protection.
Secure each removed frame, brace, or clamp in harness or containment before lowering — do not drop.
Check all bracing connections are tight and load-bearing frame stable before removing adjacent braces.
Remove clamps and connections slowly — watch for sudden frame movement or spring-back.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle upper tier until: licenced scaffolder confirms all lower bracing is secure and load-bearing capacity maintained.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not clear final components from site until: supervisor confirms all anchor points removed and all fall protection systems deactivated.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker at height is not wearing harness clipped to independent anchor.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone barricade is breached or occupants/workers are present below dismantling work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: frame movement, cracking, or instability is observed during brace removal.
admin: Confirm scaffold dismantling permit signed by licenced scaffolder before mobilising crew.
Verify exclusion zone signage in place and occupants notified of dismantling schedule.
Record completion of pre-shift toolbox on fall protection and sequence check.
Confirm all scaffold components collected and site routes clear before final handover.
ppe: Full-body harness (AS/NZS 1891.1) — class C, weight-tested within 12 months.
Lanyard with shock absorber (AS/NZS 1891.4) — length not exceeding 2m from secure anchor.
Safety helmet (Type 1, hard hat) — fitted correctly, chin strap worn.
Steel-capped boots (AS/NZS 2210.1) — ankle support, non-slip sole.
High-visibility vest or jacket — Class D minimum, visible from all ground positions.

monitoring.critical_control: Check harness clipped to independent anchor and lanyard free of tangles before each tier dismantling.
monitoring.frequency: before each worker starts elevated work, continuous visual during dismantling
monitoring.evidence: Harness tag inspection record, work log noting tier completion and anchor point secure, supervisor sign-off on hold points

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Demobilise site and reinstate building access
task_blocks_raw.scope: Remove welfare facilities, site signage, and temporary infrastructure. Clean all access routes via Kiora Lane and courtyard. Restore building entry and occupant access. Dispose of site waste
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.1 — Construction work on or adjacent to road used by traffic
hazards: Trip hazard from removal of temporary infrastructure, signage, and welfare facilities creating uneven surfaces
Vehicle strike during removal of equipment and components via Kiora Lane — traffic movement and pedestrian congestion
Dust or debris generation during site cleaning — occupant exposure during reinstatement of access
Incomplete removal or inadequate disposal of site waste — latent environmental or safety hazard
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Vehicle strike during removal of equipment and components via Kiora Lane — traffic movement and pedestrian congestion
controls: Position traffic control operator at Kiora Lane entry during all equipment removal — stop vehicle movement when pedestrians or workers cross.
Barricade access routes with temporary fencing until cleaning is complete — prevent occupants entering contaminated zones.
Sweep and wet-wipe all access routes and courtyard surfaces before opening to occupants — control dust from site materials.
Remove all welfare facility signage, barriers, and temporary infrastructure in reverse installation order — eliminate trip hazards progressively.
Segregate site waste into bins by type — dispose via licensed contractor with EPA waste receipt.
Confirm all temporary infrastructure removed and access routes clear with supervisor — hold point before occupant re-entry.
Photograph access routes and courtyard post-cleaning — verify no debris or hazards remain visible to occupants.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not restore building occupant access until: traffic management operator confirms final vehicle removal complete and Kiora Lane clear of equipment
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: pedestrians or occupants enter demobilisation zone without traffic control operator directing movement
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust or debris clouds visible during cleaning or equipment removal near occupied building entry
admin: Verify traffic control operator holds current traffic management licence — record name and licence number on site register.
Retain EPA waste contractor receipt and disposal docket — file with project WHS records.
Brief all workers on vehicle strike risk and occupant re-entry sequencing — record attendance and sign-off.
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class D) — worn during all Kiora Lane equipment removal
steel-capped footwear— grip soles to prevent slip on courtyard during wet cleaning
Dust mask (P1) — worn during dry sweeping or when dust visible

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start
monitoring.evidence: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues
